findings.claim: The verifiers' STATIC tier never reads the tool. Every EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY is a hand-written literal graded against the catalogue, never against execute(). Proof of live divergence: the declared topology carries 7 nodes including geo_0 sopimport; the tool emits 6 (no sopimport) - and verify_static still returns PASS. A regression in any tool's wiring changes nothing in the static tier. It is a documentation test wearing a verifier's name.

The LIVE tier grades only the delta of children before/after, so any damage a tool does to PRE-EXISTING nodes is structurally invisible. After scene_template + component_builder + create_variants all ran into one /stage (8 children, 4 terminal LOPs), verify_live returned PASS with an empty failure list.

The create_variants material verifier asserts a defect that does not exist, and a NEW test pins the lie. FORGE's F4 claimed copyNodesTo drops inputs; live on 22.0.368 it does not - mat_blue and mat_red both carry input ['geo_mv'] with zero errors. The verifier declares them with inputs:[] and a new test asserts that failure forever. The REAL material defect is different: 4 terminal LOPs, a dead-end, not an arity violation.

COMPOSED, second-action. The idempotency guard latches onto its own wreckage, across tools. import_megascans raises PermissionError on run 0 leaving partial state, then returns status 'already_exists' permanently on every subsequent run - it never imports anything, ever, yet reports success. Cross-tool: component_builder failing at /obj left /obj/component_wc, and the next import_megascans at /obj then returned already_exists for an asset ANOTHER tool half-built.

Failed builds orphan partial networks and the undo group does not clean up. component_builder at /obj raises hou.OperationFailed and leaves /obj/component_wc behind; scene_template into a SOP geo raises hou.InvalidInput after orphaning primitive_wc4 and camera1. hou.undos.group does not roll back.

create_variants fabricates variants of nothing and reports created. When no componentgeometry exists, base_geo stays None and the else branch creates FRESH EMPTY componentgeometry nodes. On an empty subnet: status='created', variants_created=['a','b'] - variants of nothing, no error.

create_variants pointed at a LOP network pollutes it directly. component_path='/stage' dumps geo_a, geo_b, geo_variants into /stage alongside unrelated networks and returns status='created'. The target node is never type-checked.

import_megascans cannot run at all: hou.PermissionError 'Cannot create a node inside a locked asset'. It creates SOPs directly in componentgeometry instead of its sopnet/geo child, and orphans /stage/component_mgA.
The five Solaris tools are absent from the MCP registry - zero matches for their names in _tool_registry.py. They live outside the installable package and are unreachable by any dispatch path.

set_purpose sets no purpose. No `purpose` parm exists on componentgeometry on 22.0.368; the code always falls through and still returns status='set' with an advisory note. This violates the fidelity-or-stop rule.

Solaris tools are effectively untested: pyproject testpaths=['tests'] so synapse/tests/solaris/ is NEVER collected, and it is mock-only anyway. This is the root cause of F7 and F9 surviving - a mock hou cannot raise PermissionError or report a missing parm.

verify_wiring_common's NON_LOP_TYPES exempts four types that ARE real LOPs in the pinned 218-type catalogue (null, xform, matchsize, attribwrangle). The exempt branch skips type-existence, deprecation, input-ref AND arity. Proven: two null nodes where one references ghost_node_does_not_exist returns PASS. The module's own comment that 'unknown-and-unlisted is a failure' is false for 4 of 6 entries.

check_live_network early-returns and skips the composition triad. On has_lop fail or tails != 1 it returns before terminal_no_errors / terminal_stage_resolves / stage_prim_count - so precisely the defective networks never get composition asserted.

Reserved USD names pass validation. scene_name='HoudiniLayerInfo' yields hierarchy_root '/HoudiniLayerInfo'. Both validators correctly reject '/', spaces, leading digits and empty, but have no reserved-name list.

verify_live reports FAIL on a correct no-op: a second run returns FAIL ['has_lop'] because the tool correctly returned already_exists and emitted nothing. The verifier cannot distinguish 'unchanged' from 'broken'.
import_megascans creates mtl_ref but never wires it; componentmaterial input 1 stays open and mtl_ref_asset has no consumer.
create_variants' componentgeometryvariants dead-ends with no consumer, leaving 2 terminal LOPs.
create_variants uses bare `except Exception: pass` at two sites then unconditionally returns status='created'. Failure never surfaces.
componentbuilder is absent from the live 218-type LOP catalogue; a try/except hides the native-path failure.
tool_audit is not a tool. It is a design dict in schema_tool_audit.py with no implementation module - so the relay's 'six Solaris tools' is five.
Parameter name divergence: scene_template reads `parent`, the others read `parent_path`. The mismatch silently builds into /stage instead of erroring.
terminal_no_errors is order-dependent: errors() is read before stage() cooks, so on an uncooked terminal it returns () and passes vacuously.

for_ruling.question: N6 + N7 together: did this leg deliver verification, or documentation? The static tier never reads the tool (a wiring regression changes nothing in it), and one of the 28 new green tests pins a defect that live probing REFUTES. Rule this BEFORE the register-or-quarantine question.
options: Re-derive every EXPECTED_TOPOLOGY from live emission and retire the false min_inputs pin - the verifiers become real
Accept the verifiers as documentation tests, rename them so they stop claiming to verify
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. The verifiers are close to real - they can all go red, and the live tier works. What is missing is that the static tier compares a hand-written literal against the catalogue instead of against execute(). That is a fixable seam, not a design failure. Do NOT revert: the leg's findings are the most valuable output of the whole relay.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High and compounding. 28 green tests currently certify nothing about Solaris wiring, and the greenness is actively misleading - it is the exact 'isolated-green hides composed regressions' failure the seam-gate exists to prevent.

for_ruling.question: F1 + F11: five Solaris tools are absent from the MCP registry and their tests are never collected. Is this family alive?
options: Register the tools, move their tests under tests/, repair N1-N9 - treat as an undelivered feature to finish
Quarantine the tree and strike the Phase-2 'five Solaris tools delivered' claim from the docs
for_ruling.recommendation: Decide 1-vs-2 only AFTER L2.R1. Registering tools behind vacuous verifiers is strictly worse than leaving them dead - it would make unreachable-and-broken into reachable-and-broken. If the appetite for the repair work is not there, option 2 is honest and cheap.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Medium. Nothing is reachable today, so nothing is breaking for users - the cost is a false capability claim in the docs.

for_ruling.question: N3 + N4: does a failed SYNAPSE build owe the caller a clean network? Today failures orphan partial state, and the idempotency guard then latches onto that wreckage - including another tool's wreckage - and reports success forever.
options: Yes - on exception inside the undo group, destroy the created-node set before re-raising, and make the guard verify completeness not just name-existence
No - partial state is the artist's to clean up, but the guard must still verify completeness
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1, and note this binds FAR beyond Solaris. It is a family-wide contract question about what 'undo-wrapped' actually promises. SYNAPSE's core guarantee is that every mutation is reversible; N3 shows hou.undos.group does not deliver that on the exception path.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High. This is the closest thing in the relay to a violation of SYNAPSE's stated core guarantee.

for_ruling.question: F7 doctrine: set_purpose returns status='set' having set nothing, with an advisory note. Is a success status with an advisory note ever acceptable?
options: No - fidelity-or-stop means a no-op returns a failure or a distinct status
Yes, if the note is machine-readable and the caller can branch on it
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. This is CLAUDE.md 11.6 'Fidelity = 1.0 or stop' applied literally. A success status that means 'I did nothing' is how a tool lies, and it is the same class as N6's false green.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Medium now, high once the tools are registered and an agent starts believing their return values.

for_ruling.question: N8: should the LIVE tier grade the whole network rather than only the delta of children before/after?
options: Whole network - that is the difference between a probe and a seam-gate
Delta only, plus a separate whole-network composition assertion
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 1. Delta-grading is why three tools could run into one /stage leaving 4 terminal LOPs and still return PASS with an empty failure list.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: High - it is the mechanism by which composed regressions stay invisible.

for_ruling.question: The relay cites '13/13 attacks held' from PR #48; the live runner reports 6/6 probes. Which is the acceptance unit?
options: 6 probes - what the runner actually counts
Re-express the gate in assertions and make the runner count them
for_ruling.recommendation: Option 3. The mismatch is not a regression, but a gate whose headline number cannot be reproduced by its own runner is a gate nobody can audit.
for_ruling.cost_of_delay: Low, but it is the same class of defect as L1's unsourced 18%.
